units.text: EXT. SKYLINE ROOFTOP BAR - NIGHT
Detective Annika Brandt, 40s, sits at the far end of the bar with a club soda and a view of the elevator.
She keeps her jacket on.
Under it, a wire taped below the ribs.
Her phone sits face up beside the glass.
The phone BUZZES.
She lets it ring twice, then answers and puts it to her ear.
Tell me you're up there.
units.name: HALE

units.text: Corner. By the heater. Where are you?
units.name: BRANDT

units.text: Parking structure. Level three. I'm giving it five minutes.
units.name: HALE

units.text: Five minutes is fine.
units.name: BRANDT

units.text: You come alone?
units.name: HALE

units.text: You asked me to.
units.name: BRANDT

units.text: The line goes quiet.
Wind snaps a string of lights overhead.
She watches the elevator numbers climb on the display, 2, 3, 4, and her thumb goes still on the glass.
Hale. Level three. You said that already?
units.name: BRANDT

units.text: Yeah. Why?
units.name: HALE

units.text: No reason. Come on up.
units.name: BRANDT

units.text: She ends the call.
The phone lights.
ON PHONE: unknown number -- "ur not alone up there"
She reads it once.
She does not look around.
She sets the phone face down and slides a hand into her jacket, thumbs the transmitter.
Unit two, confirm the garage camera. Level three. Is anyone there?
units.name: BRANDT

units.text: A beat.
Nothing in the earpiece.
Static, then a CLICK.
The elevator DINGS.
Tomasz Hale, 50s, rumpled suit, steps out and scans the roof.
He sees her, hesitates, then crosses to the stool beside hers.
He sits too carefully, as though the cushion might be wired.
You look like a cop.
units.name: HALE

units.text: You look like a man who's late.
units.name: BRANDT

units.text: I wasn't in the garage.
units.name: HALE

units.text: She turns her head.
Say that again.
units.name: BRANDT

units.text: I took the stairs. I was on the stairs the whole time. The call, it wasn't me calling.
units.name: HALE

units.text: Her phone BUZZES against the bar.
She doesn't touch it.
He nods at it.
That's him. He's got my phone. He's got my kid's school schedule too, Detective, that was the part I couldn't, I had to come.
units.name: HALE

units.text: Who has your phone?
units.name: BRANDT

units.text: The man at the table behind you. Blue shirt. Don't turn around.
units.name: HALE

units.text: The ice in her glass shifts.
Somewhere behind her a chair scrapes.
ON PHONE: unknown number -- "good. now both of u stand up"
How long has he been sitting there?
units.name: BRANDT

units.text: Since before I got here. He walked me up.
units.name: HALE

units.text: And the garage?
units.name: BRANDT

units.text: There's no one in the garage. There's never been anyone. He wanted you to say it out loud.
units.name: HALE

units.text: She exhales.
Her hand comes out of the jacket empty.
Behind her, a glass is set down, softly, and a shadow lengthens across the bar top.
Then he's already heard everything.
units.name: BRANDT

units.text: Every word.
units.name: HALE

units.text: The phone BUZZES a third time.
Neither of them looks at it.
She slides off the stool, standing straight, still not turning around.
He stays seated, staring into his lap.
Stay seated, Tomasz. Whatever happens next, you stay in that chair.
units.name: BRANDT

units.text: What are you going to do?
units.name: HALE

units.text: She lifts the wire's transmitter out from under her shirt in plain view and lays it on the bar.
Say hello.
units.name: BRANDT

units.text: She turns around.
